script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The passage does not say whether the disciples were expecting Jesus.
The passage does not say that Jesus’ hands and side were all the disciples needed to look at.
“A minute earlier” adds a time interval the passage does not give. The doorbell line also puts a modern object in the Bible scene.
The passage says the disciples rejoiced, but it does not say that nobody argued or debated.
The claim that nobody can be sent while staying behind a locked door adds a condition Jesus does not state.
The prediction that the locked doors were about to have less to do with their day goes beyond what this passage says.
The explanation repeats the answer without adding much insight or Papa Dorin’s personality.
Quoting Thomas’s refusal without its condition makes it sound unconditional. The explanation then reduces his stated conditions to seeing for himself, omitting what he said about touching.
Quoting “I will never believe” without Thomas’s condition makes his statement sound unconditional.
The explanation repeats that Thomas was specific without adding insight or a distinct Papa Dorin voice.
The passage says the next meeting was eight days later, not that Thomas had waited eight days.
Saying the blessing “also” reaches those who have not seen implies Jesus said those who saw Him were blessed. Here He specifically calls blessed those who have not seen and yet have believed.
